quotes.text: Workflow's agent equals intent to automation for common Microsoft 365 work. Power automate equals enterprise grade, durable automation for complex, long-running, governed processes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the episode's core distinction between the two automation tools into one comparison.

quotes.text: Agent reduces configuration errors by refusing to let you micromanage every field. Fewer knobs, fewer misalignments. Power automate minimizes runtime errors through explicit rules, retries and idempotency.

takeaways: Workflows agent builds common Microsoft 365 automations like simple approvals, notifications and task creation from natural language far faster than Power Automate.
Power Automate remains the right engine for long-running, multi-branch or regulated processes that need retries, idempotency, SLAs and audit trails.
The best pattern is hybrid: the agent captures context conversationally and hands off to a Power Automate flow for durable, governed execution under aligned DLP and environments.
hook: Are you still hand-wiring every approval and notification in Power Automate? This episode compares the Workflows agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot with Power Automate across five real use cases for makers and IT admins. You get a clear rule for what to keep, what to move and how to govern a hybrid setup.
